title: Locating pitch classes on the neck
description: Practice deriving any note from the open string and the E–F / B–C half steps.

cards.front: How do you locate a pitch class on a given string?
cards.back: Start from the open string, count half steps (frets) up, and use the E–F and B–C half-step pairs to know where accidentals do and do not occur.

cards.front: On one string, how often does each pitch class appear in frets 0–11? What about fret 12?
cards.back: Exactly once in frets 0–11. Fret 12 repeats the open string’s class, one octave higher.

cards.front: The natural-fret table comes from which two facts you already know?
cards.back: One fret is one half step, and the naturals run W W H W W W H (half steps at E–F and B–C).

cards.front: Derive the natural frets on string 6 from open E.
Name the naturals and frets on string 6 (open E).
Name the naturals and frets on string 5 (open A).
Name the naturals and frets on string 4 (open D).
Name the naturals and frets on string 3 (open G).
Name the naturals and frets on string 2 (open B).
What is the note layout of string 1 compared with string 6?
cards.back: Identical classes (both E strings), two octaves apart: E 0, F 1, G 3, and so on.

cards.front: Where do sharps and flats sit relative to the naturals?
cards.back: On the frets between the naturals. On string 5, C♯/D♭ is fret 4 (between C at 3 and D at 5).

cards.front: Find F♯ on string 4 by counting from the open string.
cards.back: Open D (0), E (2), F (3), then one fret above F → fret 4.

cards.front: String 5 fret 9 is F♯. Where is that same F♯ on string 4?
cards.back: Five frets lower: fret 4. The five-frets-lower rule holds for every adjacent pair except 3 to 2 (four frets).

cards.front: Name the main landmarks that speed up note finding.
cards.back: Fret 5 matches the next thinner open string (fret 4 on string 3). Fret 12 repeats the open class. After E or B, the next fret is a natural (F or C). Strings 6 and 1 share a layout.

cards.front: If you are on E or B, what is the next fret up?
cards.back: A natural: F after E, C after B — not a sharp.

What note is string 5 fret 7?
What note is string 4 fret 9?
What note is string 3 fret 4?
What note is string 2 fret 6?
Find every C in frets 0–12 on all six strings.
Find every A in frets 0–12 on all six strings.
Find F♯ on each string within frets 0–12.
If you cannot recall a fret instantly, what should you do?
cards.back: Run the derivation from the open string. Counting is slower than recall but always correct, and it trains the structure until recall is automatic.
